edges.description: Constitutive RET phosphorylation activates multiple signaling pathways
Sustained signaling drives transformation of thyroid C-cells and chromaffin cells

edges.source: Avoidance of Agents Precipitating Pheochromocytoma Crisis

nodes.description: Dopamine D2 receptor antagonists (including antiemetics such as metoclopramide) and beta-adrenergic receptor antagonists given without prior alpha-blockade carry a high risk of adverse reactions in an individual with an unresected pheochromocytoma, and are avoided until pheochromocytoma has been excluded or resected.
nodes.id: Avoidance of Agents Precipitating Pheochromocytoma Crisis

evidence.snippet: Dopamine D2 receptor antagonists and beta-adrenergic receptor antagonists present a high risk for adverse reactions in individuals with pheochromocytoma.

nodes.description: Constitutively active RET phosphorylates intracellular substrates and activates RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT, and JAK-STAT signaling pathways. These promote cell proliferation, survival, and transformation of neuroendocrine cell populations.

evidence.snippet: RET can activate various signaling pathways such as RAS/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT, p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) pathways.

nodes.description: Constitutive RET signaling drives transformation of neuroendocrine cell populations. C-cell hyperplasia precedes MTC development and serves as a preneoplastic lesion. Similar processes affect adrenal chromaffin cells leading to pheochromocytoma.

evidence.reference_title: Management of medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN2 syndromes in childhood.
evidence.snippet: it frequently occurs secondary to activating mutations in the RET proto-oncogene and arises from pre-existing C-cell hyperplasia.

nodes.description: Pheochromocytomas occur in approximately 50% of MEN2A and MEN2B patients. Often bilateral (50-80%) and may be diagnosed before, concurrent with, or after MTC. Screening with plasma metanephrines is essential before any surgery. Generally benign but can cause hypertensive crises if undiagnosed.

evidence.snippet: MEN2A and MEN2B involve an increased risk for pheochromocytoma

nodes.description: Germline activating mutations in RET cause ligand-independent, constitutive tyrosine kinase activation. The route differs by subtype: MEN2A extracellular-cysteine alleles activate the kinase by forming disulfide-bonded homodimers, while the MEN2B M918T kinase-domain allele activates without forming dimers. Unlike tumor suppressor syndromes, only one mutant allele is required (no second hit). This represents a gain-of-function oncogene mechanism.

biological_processes: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway

evidence.snippet: identification of a heterozygous germline gain-of-function variant in RET on molecular genetic testing.

evidence.reference_title: Full activation of MEN2B mutant RET by an additional MEN2A mutation or by ligand GDNF stimulation.
evidence.snippet: In MEN2A mutations affecting cysteine residues in the extracellular domain of the receptor cause constitutive activation of the tyrosine kinase by the formation of disulfide-bonded homodimers.

evidence.reference_title: Full activation of MEN2B mutant RET by an additional MEN2A mutation or by ligand GDNF stimulation.
evidence.snippet: This mutation does not lead to dimer formation, but has been shown (both biologically and biochemically) to cause ligand-independent activation of the Ret protein

nodes.description: C-cell hyperplasia progresses to medullary thyroid carcinoma. The age of MTC onset correlates with mutation location and aggressiveness. MEN2B mutations (M918T) cause earliest onset, often in infancy, while some FMTC mutations may not cause MTC until adulthood.

evidence.snippet: MTC typically occurs in early childhood in MEN2B, early adulthood in MEN2A, and middle age in FMTC.

evidence.reference_title: Management of medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN2 syndromes in childhood.
evidence.snippet: Strong genotype-phenotype correlations have facilitated the development of guidelines for interventions.
